title: Impact of Upwind Pollution on Infant Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS), using wind direction–based upwind indicator z as an instrument for pollution exposure x.
- Why: x (pollution) is likely endogenous due to omitted determinants of infant health (e.g., unobserved neighborhood health risks) and measurement error. Wind direction creates quasi-random variation in x via z that is plausibly exogenous to infant health, enabling identification of the causal effect of x on y.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: z affects pollution exposure (Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0). We will check with the first-stage F-statistic and partial R^2.
  - Exclusion: Conditional on controls, z affects infant mortality only via pollution exposure (no direct impact of being upwind on mortality aside from pollution exposure).
  - Independence: z is as good as randomly assigned conditional on controls (e.g., wind realizations not systematically related to unobserved infant health determinants).
  - Monotonicity: Upwind status does not reduce exposure for some units while increasing it for others (no defiers).
  - SUTVA and stable relationships over the sample.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis (2SLS IV)
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CI, p-value)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Load packages (install if needed)
needed_pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest", "car")
to_install <- needed_pkgs[!sapply(needed_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)
  library(sandwich)
  library(lmtest)
  library(car)
})

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s75_data.csv")
df <- na.omit(df)

# Sanity check: columns
stopifnot(all(c("y","x","z","controls") %in% names(df)))

# 2) Naive OLS (for comparison)
ols_mod <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_vcov <- vcovHC(ols_mod, type = "HC1")
ols_ct <- coeftest(ols_mod, vcov = ols_vcov)

# 3) First stage and instrument strength
fs_mod_controls <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
fs_mod_full     <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)

# Robust F-test for excluded instrument(s): compare models with and without z
fs_wald <- waldtest(fs_mod_full, fs_mod_controls, vcov = vcovHC(fs_mod_full, type = "HC1"), test = "F")
fs_F    <- as.numeric(fs_wald[2, "F"])
fs_p    <- as.numeric(fs_wald[2, "Pr(>F)"])

# Partial R^2 of instrument(s) given controls
R2_full <- summary(fs_mod_full)$r.squared
R2_ctrl <- summary(fs_mod_controls)$r.squared
partial_R2 <- (R2_full - R2_ctrl) / (1 - R2_ctrl)

# 4) Reduced-form (effect of z on y)
rf_mod <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
rf_ct  <- coeftest(rf_mod, vcov = vcovHC(rf_mod, type = "HC1"))

# 5) 2SLS IV: y ~ x + controls | z + controls
iv_mod <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = iv_vcov)

# Extract key IV results for x
iv_beta <- iv_ct["x", "Estimate"]
iv_se   <- iv_ct["x", "Std. Error"]
iv_t    <- iv_ct["x", "t value"]
iv_p    <- iv_ct["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]
df_res  <- iv_mod$df.residual
tcrit   <- qt(0.975, df = df_res)
iv_ci_l <- iv_beta - tcrit * iv_se
iv_ci_u <- iv_beta + tcrit * iv_se

# 6) Robustness checks
# 6a) IV without controls
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_noc_ct <- coeftest(iv_noc, vcov = vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC1"))
iv_noc_beta <- iv_noc_ct["x", "Estimate"]
iv_noc_se   <- iv_noc_ct["x", "Std. Error"]

# 6b) Add nonlinear control (controls^2)
df$controls_sq <- df$controls^2
iv_poly <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls_sq | z + controls + controls_sq, data = df)
iv_poly_ct <- coeftest(iv_poly, vcov = vcovHC(iv_poly, type = "HC1"))
iv_poly_beta <- iv_poly_ct["x", "Estimate"]
iv_poly_se   <- iv_poly_ct["x", "Std. Error"]

# 6c) Report naive OLS coefficient on x (for endogeneity direction)
ols_beta <- ols_ct["x", "Estimate"]
ols_se   <- ols_ct["x", "Std. Error"]

# 6d) Print reduced-form and first-stage slopes on z
rf_beta_z <- rf_ct["z", "Estimate"]
rf_se_z   <- rf_ct["z", "Std. Error"]
fs_ct     <- coeftest(fs_mod_full, vcov = vcovHC(fs_mod_full, type = "HC1"))
fs_beta_z <- fs_ct["z", "Estimate"]
fs_se_z   <- fs_ct["z", "Std. Error"]

# 7) Output
cat("Main IV result (2SLS, HC1-robust):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effect of pollution (x) on infant mortality (y): %.4f\n", iv_beta))
cat(sprintf("  Std. Error: %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f] | p-value: %.4g\n\n", iv_se, iv_ci_l, iv_ci_u, iv_p))

cat("Instrument strength (first stage):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Robust F-stat for excluded instrument(s) (z): %.2f (p = %.4g)\n", fs_F, fs_p))
cat(sprintf("  First-stage coefficient on z: %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n", fs_beta_z, fs_se_z))
cat(sprintf("  Partial R^2 of z | controls: %.4f\n\n", partial_R2))

cat("Reduced-form (y on z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coefficient on z: %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n\n", rf_beta_z, rf_se_z))

cat("Robustness checks:\n")
cat(sprintf("  IV without controls: beta_x = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n", iv_noc_beta, iv_noc_se))
cat(sprintf("  IV with controls and controls^2: beta_x = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n", iv_poly_beta, iv_poly_se))
cat(sprintf("  Naive OLS (y ~ x + controls): beta_x = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n", ols_beta, ols_se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Higher pollution exposure should increase infant mortality, so the 2SLS coefficient on x is expected to be > 0.
- Magnitude: With standardized-like variables in the preview, I expect a meaningful elasticity: roughly 0.3–0.8 increase in infant mortality (in y units) per 1-unit increase in pollution exposure. The IV estimate may exceed OLS if OLS suffers attenuation from measurement error in x or be larger/smaller depending on selection bias direction.
- Diagnostics: A strong first-stage (robust F > 10 and partial R^2 in the several-percent range or higher) would support instrument relevance. Consistent signs between reduced-form (z → y) and first-stage (z → x) would corroborate the exclusion pathway.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Wind direction is used as an instrument for pollution exposure.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Upwind pollution exposure is found to significantly increase infant mortality.
